title: Income Tax Act 2023 3rd Schedule Part 1 – Tax VAT Point
main_content: Third Schedule - Depreciation allowance, depletion allowance and amortization [Notes to Sections 42, 49 and 50] Part 1 - Calculation of depreciation allowance Depreciation allowance on assets used in agriculture.- (1) Depreciation allowance in respect of any capital asset, works or physical infrastructure owned by a taxpayer used for agricultural purposes shall be paid on the depreciated value at the rate prescribed in the table below, namely:- Table Serial No. Capital assets Rate of Depreciation 1 Buildings or structures constructed of brick, concrete, steel or similar materials 5 2 Houses constructed of tin, bamboo, thatch or similar materials 10 3 Permanent fence 10 4 Tube well 10 5 Tank 10 6 Irrigation wells, channels, pipes 10 7 Agricultural implements made of wood or bamboo 10 8 Weighing machine 10 9 Tractors, oil engines and light machinery 10 10 Trucks, delivery vans and other motor vehicles 10 11 Piper pumping equipment 20 12 Non-Mechanized Van 15 13 Steam engine 10 14 Factory machinery 15 15 Such general machinery, tools, plant  and other assets not mentioned in this table 10 (2) Where in any income year any such capital asset, plant or physical infrastructure is not wholly used for agricultural purposes of the taxpayer, the depreciation allowance allowed under sub-section (1) for that income Year shall be the amount of depreciation allowance allowed if the said asset was wholly used for agricultural purposes, shall be payable at its reasonable proportional rate. 2. Depreciation allowance on assets used in business.— (1) Depreciation allowance for the relevant income year on any asset used by a taxpayer for business purposes and owned by him shall be granted on the basis, rates and limitations, qualifications and conditions set out in this Part. (2) The depreciation allowance referred to in sub-section (1) shall be the ordinary depreciation allowance and the initial depreciation allowance for the relevant income year on any asset used by the taxpayer for business purposes and owned by him, and shall be on the depreciated value of the said asset at the basis, rate, subject to limitations, qualifications and conditions. (3) Where such asset is not wholly used for the purpose of the business of the taxpayer in any income year, the depreciation allowance allowed under sub-section (1) for that income year shall be payable at a reasonable proportionate rate of the amount of depreciation allowance which would have been allowed if the asset had been wholly used for the purpose of the business. (4) Depreciation allowance shall not be payable on any asset under this section, unless the return of the taxpayer reflects a claim that the asset is used for business purposes. (5) Where the asset is not fully used for business purposes, in calculating the depreciated value of the said asset, the asset shall be deemed to have been fully used for business purposes. (6) The total deduction allowed against any asset shall not exceed the purchase price of the said asset. (7) Depreciation of assets owned by a particular leasing company and leased to any other person shall be deductible only against the lease rental income arising from such assets. (8) No allowance shall be payable by the lessor under this section in favor of any particular company or establishment in respect of any such machinery, plant, vehicle or furniture which has been given on finance lease to any lessee. (9) No allowance shall be admissible under this section if- (a) fails to furnish particulars prescribed by the Board or other information and documents required by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes while filing the return; and (b) Similar assets are not used in the relevant income year. (10) For the purposes of this section, ‘specified leasing company’ means a leasing company, banking company or any other financial institution engaged in the business of lease. 3. Determination of purchase price of an asset.- (1) The purchase price of a motor vehicle of a taxpayer shall be deemed to be more than 30 (thirty) lakhs if the said depreciation allowance is payable for any passenger motor vehicle other than a bus or minibus used for the transportation of students, teachers or employees of the taxpayer’s business establishment. (2) In computing the purchase price of an asset, the value of any allowance, subsidy, rebate or commission and assistance (other than interest-bearing or interest-free loans) received by the taxpayer from the Government or any authority or person shall be excluded. (3) Where the taxpayer acquires any used assets other than those mentioned in sub-section (1), the acquisition value of the said asset shall not exceed its fair market value. (4) Where the acquisition of an asset involves a foreign currency loan or foreign currency exposure, the acquisition value of an asset shall be calculated after making the following adjustments, namely:- (a) including exchange rate fluctuation losses or exchange rate hedging expenses; (b) net of exchange rate gains. 4. Rate of Normal Depreciation Allowance.- Normal depreciation allowance shall be calculated on the depreciated value of an asset at the rate specified in the table below, namely:- Table Serial No. Class of assets Rate (on depreciated value %) 1 Building (unless otherwise specified in this table) 5 2 Factory building 10 3 Furniture and fittings 10 4 Office equipment 10 5 Machinery, Plant and Equipment (unless otherwise specified in this Schedule) seagoing ship 10 6 Seagoing ship (a) New 5 (b) Old at the time of purchase whose age- i) Not more than 10 years 10 ii) 10 years or more 20 7 X-ray, electrotherapeutic and other medical equipment including its spare parts 20 8 Battery operated apparatus and rechargeable batteries 30 9 Equipment used for production and display of audio-visual products 20 10 All types of motor vehicles except those driven on hire 10 11 All types of motor vehicles driven on hire 20 12 Computer hardware including printers, monitors and ancillary items 25 13 Professional and reference books 25 14 Aircraft, aeroengines and aerial photographic equipment 30 15 Molds used for making glass or plastic products or concrete pipes 30 16 Related to mineral oil a) Equipment installed under ground 100 b) Other above ground equipment including portable boilers, drilling rigs, wellhead tanks and rigs 25 17 Bridge 2 18 Road 2 19 Flyover 2 20 Pavement Runway, Taxiway 2.5 21 Apron, Tarmac 2.5 22 Boarding Bridge 10 23 Communication and search aids and other tools 5 24 All such physical resources not mentioned in this table 10 5. Initial depreciation allowance. (1) Where a building is newly constructed or an asset including machinery or plant is used in Bangladesh for the first time, initial depreciation allowance shall be allowed at the rate specified in sub-section (4), subject to the limits and conditions set out in this section. (2) No initial depreciation allowance shall be allowed in respect of the following assets, namely:- (a) Such motor vehicle not hired, and (b) Any such machinery or installation previously used in Bangladesh (3) Initial depreciation allowance shall be allowed in respect of the income year in which any assets is first used by a taxpayer for the purposes of his trade or profession or in the income year in which commercial production is first commenced, whichever occurs later. (4) Initial depreciation allowance shall be calculated on the purchase price of the asset concerned at the rate specified in the table below, namely – Table Serial No. Assets Rate of Initial depreciation 1 2 3 1 Any type of building 10% 2 any assets covered under “plant or machinery” other than vessels or motor vehicles for hire 25% 6. Accelerated depreciation allowance on plant or machinery.- (1) Where any asset covered by machinery or plant is used in any industrial establishment situated in Bangladesh, accelerated depreciation allowance shall be allowed at the rate specified in sub-section (3), subject to the limits and conditions set out in this section. (2) Accelerated depreciation allowance shall be allowed up to 3 (three) years from the year of commencement of commercial production of the industrial establishment. (3) Accelerated depreciation shall be calculated on the purchase price of the asset concerned at the rate specified in the table below, namely:- Table Serial No. Income year of Commencement of Commercial Production Accelerate depreciation Rate 1 2 3 1 First income year 50% 2 Second income year 30% 3 Third income year 20% (4) Allowance of accelerated depreciation shall be allowed subject to the following conditions, limits and qualifications, namely:- (a) the relevant resource is owned by the industrial establishment referred to in sub-paragraph (1) and has not previously been used in Bangladesh; (b) Ownership and management of industrial establishments (i) governed by any law for the time being in force or by a body corporate established under the law having its head office in Bangladesh; or (ii) carried on by a company as defined in the Companies Act, 1994 (Act No. 18 of 1994) having its registered office in Bangladesh and having an authorized and paid-up capital of at least 20 (twenty) lakhs on the date of commencement of commercial production; (c) The industrial establishment- (i) TIN holder; (ii) maintain accounts in accordance with the provisions of this Act; (iii) keep separate and distinct accounts; (iv) file returns in accordance with the provisions of this Act; (d) by following the procedure described below, namely:- (i) apply to the Board, in the prescribed form and manner, for accelerated depreciation allowance within 6 (six) months from the last day of the month of commencement of commercial production; (ii) The application shall be accompanied by a declaration to the effect that the industrial establishment is not exempted from tax under any section of this Act, and has not and will not make any application to the Board for exemption from tax. (5) If accelerated depreciation allowance is allowed on any asset in Act shall be allowed in favor of that asset. 7. Provisions relating to sale or transfer of assets and gain or loss thereon.- Where any asset is sold or transferred by a taxpayer in any income year, no depreciation allowance under this Part shall be allowed in that income year against such asset. 8. Explanation.- For the purposes of this section- (1) “asset” means tangible movable property owned by a person, immovable property (other than unused land), or structural improvements on immovable property- (a) whose normal useful life exceeds 1 (one) year; (b) which is reduced in value or rendered unusable by normal use; and (c) for which no allowance other than depreciation allowance is admissible under any provision of this Act; (2) “furniture” shall include fittings; (3) “establishment” shall include vessels, vehicles, books, scientific instruments, and surgical instruments used for business purposes; (4) “vessel” shall include any steamer, motor vessel, sail, tug boat, steel or iron barge for cargo, wooden cargo boat, motor launch and speed boat; (5) “structural development” (in relation to immovable property), means any building, road, driveway, car park, railway line, pipe line, bridge, tunnel, airport runway, canal, dock, wharf, retaining wall, fence, power line;, shall include water or drainage pipes, drains, landscaping or dams; (6) “depreciated value” means- (a) in case the asset is acquired in any income year, the purchase price of the asset deducting any initial allowance allowed in respect of the asset; (b) in other cases, from the purchase value of the asset deducting the sum of the depreciation allowances allowed against the asset in the tax assessment for the preceding income year or years.
